grades.quote: On a POSIX system (such as Linux or Mac OS X), demonstrate a program continuing to make use of an open file after all names for that file have been removed.
grades.reason: Describes the behavior and suggests a demonstration, but does not explain why the file remains accessible.

grades.quote: iput() doesn’t truncate a file immediately when the link count for the file drops to zero, because some process might still hold a reference to the inode in memory
grades.reason: Directly explains that an existing reference prevents deletion after the last link disappears.

grades.quote: The unlink system call removes a name from the file system. The file’s inode and the disk space holding its content are only freed when the file’s link count is zero and no file descriptors refer to it.
grades.reason: Directly explains why an open descriptor retains access after unlink removes the name.
Shows that open-then-unlink preserves an unnamed inode until the descriptor closes or the process exits.
